chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Hamad ibn Uthman, from Khalaf ibn Hamad, from Rib'i, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the people engage in disobedience to Allah, the Exalted and Glorious, if they are riders, they are the cavalry of Iblees, and if they are on foot, they are his infantry.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of a community that disobeys Allah?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the concept of collective spiritual alignment, where a group's unified disobedience transforms them into the literal 'army of Iblees,' regardless of their physical state. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the metaphysical reality of the 'Jund' (army) of Satan, linking individual sins to a broader cosmic battle between divine and evil forces. The imagery underscores that sin is not merely an isolated act but a mobilization of the self against God.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 5. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Muhammad b. Ali al-Kufi from Muhammad b. Sinan from Hamad b. Uthman from Khalaf b. Hamad from Rib’i from al-Fudhayl b. Yasar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
When some people of a community start disobeying Allah, they will be the army of Iblees whether they ride or walk.”
